title: Use execution and profiling feedback as a bounded candidate-generation loop

source.title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels?
source.claim_scope: Benchmark evidence that execution and profiling feedback can improve iterative refinement; it does not identify a universally best search policy.

implementation_recipe: Generate several architecture-distinct candidates before giving any one candidate multiple tuning rounds.
Feed compile, correctness, timing, and a compact bottleneck summary back into the next proposal.
Stop a local line after bounded failures and return to a different opportunity or architecture family.
validation_recipe: Track time to first correct candidate, time to first improvement, and best result at fixed wall-clock budgets.
Report correctness-plus-speed thresholds across all tasks or workload cases, not only successful examples.
Separate technical repair failures from causal performance failures.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Profiling should redirect search when an intended optimization moves the bottleneck elsewhere.
Portfolio-level progress can improve even when individual candidate lines terminate earlier.
failure_modes: The agent repeatedly tunes launch parameters after the measured bottleneck has moved.
Feedback is too verbose or unstructured to change the next architecture decision.
The search overfits a public anchor input.
scope_limits: Benchmark success rates do not predict success on a specific production operator.
More feedback rounds are not a substitute for architecture diversity.

candidate_archetypes.name: bounded architecture portfolio
candidate_archetypes.template: Give each distinct family one build/correctness/smoke attempt, halve the portfolio, and spend deeper analysis only on survivors.
